definitions.meaning: a dishonest scheme or swindle, as in a protection scam

explanation.surface: Shady dealing leads to a public outcry.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindling scheme is a racket in slang, and a din or loud noise is a racket too.

parts.note: the rest means the remaining ones, the others
rain is water falling from the sky

explanation.surface: Someone checks whether the rest of the group have something to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To check someone is to hold them back, a synonym of curbing them.

definitions.meaning: what a book or document deals with, listed on its opening page
a verb: pleases or satisfies someone

explanation.surface: The topic under discussion is a pleasing one.
explanation.definitionFit: A book's subject matter is what it holds within, and a thing that satisfies someone pleases them in the verb sense.

clue.text: Regret raising old money in France

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising means the word regret's synonym is written from bottom to top

parts.note: to rue something is to regret it

explanation.surface: Someone laments that the old French franc is being brought back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' turns RUE upwards to give EUR, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The euro is the currency used in France since it replaced the franc.

clue.text: In emergency, move slowly after a knock

indicators.note: the inching motion comes after the knock in the finished word

parts.note: a tap is a light knock
to inch is to creep forward a little at a time

explanation.surface: After a blow to the head someone can only shuffle along, so it is an emergency.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means if absolutely necessary, as a last resort in an urgent situation.

clue.text: Carpentry's an odd thing to project

indicators.note: odd suggests the letters of carpentry's an are in a strange, jumbled order

explanation.surface: Woodwork is said to be a peculiar thing to stick out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' is the anagram signal: it rearranges CARPENTRYSAN, the letters of 'Carpentry's an'.
explanation.definitionFit: A slide or film image put up on a screen with a projector is called a transparency.

indicators.note: in a down clue an ascent means the mountain's word is read upwards, bottom to top

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain, as in Switzerland

explanation.surface: Someone draws up a scheme for climbing a northern peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ascent' turns NALP upwards, as this is a down clue; 'for' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme and a plan are synonyms, both meaning a worked-out course of action.

clue.text: Mug one may put one's teeth into?

definitions.meaning: slang for a fool or a gullible person, also for the head

definitions.text: one may put one's teeth into?
definitions.meaning: something edible you bite, such as a strip of pasta

explanation.surface: A drinking cup that someone might bite on.
explanation.definitionFit: A noodle is slang for a simpleton or the head, and also a strip of pasta that one bites into.

parts.note: a race is a contest of speed

explanation.surface: A title is needed for an inter-house contest, as at a school sports day.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's first name, as borne by the Roman poet, so an example of a name.

parts.note: sent means dispatched, sent off

explanation.surface: A security officer was sent off by train.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry is a soldier posted on watch, an example of a guard.

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
an amour is a love affair

explanation.surface: A mistress features in a typical extramarital liaison.
explanation.definitionFit: A paramour is an illicit lover, and a kept woman is a mistress supported by her lover.

clue.text: Presumably it's of the first water

definitions.text: Presumably it's of the first water

parts.words: Presumably it's of the first water
parts.note: of the first water is an idiom for of the highest quality, here read literally as a body of water ranking top

explanation.surface: Something is presumed to be of the very finest quality, like a flawless diamond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of the first water' is a jeweller's phrase for the best grade of gem; taken literally, the top-ranking water is a great North American lake whose name means higher.
explanation.definitionFit: This North American lake's name says it is the higher or better one, hence a water of the first rank.

indicators.note: back tells us to read the synonym of look from right to left

parts.note: to leer is to look slyly or lecherously

explanation.surface: Someone glances over their shoulder and feels giddy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LEER round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To reel is to stagger or feel the world spin, as when giddy.

clue.text: Dad has to work in break

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
to use something is to make it work, operate it

explanation.surface: Father has to get back to his job during the interval.
explanation.definitionFit: A pause is a short stop or rest, a synonym of a break.

clue.text: Smart fellow the French take into acount

indicators.note: the French article is taken into the abbreviation for account, placed within it

parts.note: AC is short for account; the clue misspells the word
le is a French word for the

explanation.surface: A clever chap gets the French involved in the reckoning.
explanation.walkthrough: A smart alec is a know-all; the name alone stands for the type.
explanation.definitionFit: From the phrase smart alec, a cocky know-all; the name by itself is the fellow.

indicators.note: the politician goes into the jumbled letters
clumsy suggests the word lie is awkwardly mangled into a new order

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician is pressured into telling a poorly crafted untruth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clumsy' makes IEL from the lie, and 'into' places the politician after its first letter. 'Force' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or push someone to act, which is to force them.

explanation.surface: The wreckage left behind after fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrap means leftover fragments or waste, and also, informally, a brawl or fight.

clue.text: Breaking the cane after being angry indicates lack of restraint

indicators.note: the broken cane comes after the angry phrase in the answer

parts.note: in a temper means angry

indicators.note: breaking suggests the word cane is smashed and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: Snapping a cane in a fury shows a person has no self-control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking' makes ANCE; 'the' is only a link. 'Being angry' must be read as the phrase in a temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Intemperance is excess or overindulgence, especially in drink, a failure of self-control.

indicators.note: the drunk word comes before the dance in the answer

parts.note: high means intoxicated
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Someone has a mixed drink before going to the dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A highball is a spirit served with a mixer in a tall glass, a type of mixed drink.

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
ease means comfort or freedom from strain

explanation.surface: A rise in someone's bank balance brings comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: A gain and an increase are synonyms, both meaning a growth in amount.

indicators.note: off suggests the letters of roman retinue are disordered, off their proper arrangement

explanation.surface: An instruction to pay off the attendants of a Roman lord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' is the anagram signal: it rearranges the twelve letters of 'Roman retinue'.
explanation.definitionFit: Remuneration is payment for work done, a formal synonym of pay.

clue.text: Who had ordered a seat on a jumbo?

indicators.note: ordered suggests the letters of who had are arranged into a new sequence

explanation.surface: A question asking who booked a seat on a jumbo jet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges the letters of 'Who had'. 'Jumbo' suggests an airliner, but here it is an elephant.
explanation.definitionFit: A howdah is a canopied seat carried on an elephant's back, and Jumbo is a famous elephant's name.

clue.text: One who treats vile disorder and rot

parts.note: a doctor treats patients; DR is short for doctor

indicators.note: disorder suggests the word vile is jumbled up

explanation.surface: A physician treats a nasty illness and decay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorder' makes IVEL. 'Rot' looks like decay to go with disease, but here it means nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Rot here means nonsense, and drivel is silly talk or rubbish.

indicators.note: the note sits in the middle of the currency word

parts.note: the öre is a coin of Sweden, the øre of Denmark and Norway
G is a musical note

explanation.surface: A monstrous figure appears on a Nordic banknote.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a man-eating giant in folklore, an example of a monster.

clue.text: A rod, or what one may get with it

definitions.meaning: an old unit of length, five and a half yards

definitions.text: what one may get with it
definitions.meaning: a freshwater fish one might catch with a fishing rod

explanation.surface: A fishing rod, or the catch it might bring.
explanation.definitionFit: A perch is an old measure equal to a rod or pole, and also a freshwater fish an angler catches.

definitions.meaning: British slang for a cup of tea

explanation.surface: Fish served at teatime.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAR is old British slang for tea, from the Chinese word cha.
explanation.definitionFit: The char is a cold-water fish related to trout, and in British slang char is a cuppa.

clue.text: Request to remain true to type?

definitions.text: Request to remain true to type?

parts.words: Request to remain true to type?
parts.note: a proofreader's mark asking that a crossed-out piece of printed type be left standing, true to the original

explanation.surface: A plea for someone to stay faithful to their character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'True to type' sounds like staying in character, but the type is printer's type: the Latin word means let it stand.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin proofreading instruction tells the printer to ignore a correction and keep the original wording.

parts.note: Pat, short for Patrick, is a stereotypical Irish name
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: An Irish detective is close behind his quarry.
explanation.definitionFit: A path is a track or way to walk along, a synonym of a trail.

clue.text: Perfectly fit emblem of peace to follow

parts.note: a dove, often with an olive branch, symbolises peace
to tail someone is to follow them closely

explanation.surface: A symbol of peace that fits flawlessly comes next.
explanation.definitionFit: To dovetail is to join neatly together, like interlocking woodworking joints.

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means the girl's name is placed next to the vessel, here after it

parts.note: a can is a container or vessel
Ada is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A rural lass is aboard the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Wordplay reads ADA on CAN, which gives CAN then ADA.
explanation.definitionFit: This nation is a North American country, north of the United States.

clue.text: Injury of outside left when fouled is a break

indicators.note: the injury word goes outside the jumbled letters, wrapping them

parts.note: harm is injury or damage

indicators.note: fouled suggests the word left is tangled up into a new order

explanation.surface: A football winger's injury from a foul means a spell on the sidelines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when fouled' makes LFTE and 'outside' wraps the injury round it. The football picture misleads: in Britain, half term is a short school holiday in the middle of a term.
explanation.definitionFit: Half term is a short school holiday in Britain, a break between lessons.

clue.text: Put off by girl wanting love but no ring

parts.note: she refers to a female, a girl

indicators.note: no tells us the ring shape is dropped from the word love

parts.note: love is taken as written
O looks like a ring

explanation.surface: A lovelorn girl is shunned because she has no ring on her finger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' means desiring, so SHE wants LOVE; 'no' removes the ring, O, leaving LVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To shelve a plan is to postpone it, so to put it off.
